messages.subject: mirt versus robust linear
parts:
Dear Phil,
thanks a lot for writing mirt, very useful and excellent tool...
I fitted 6-factor IRT model (graded response, MHRM).
Fit indices, especially SRMSR and RMSEA are very different in comparison
with robust linear methods (I supposed it, of course).
AIC and BIC of mirt models is always better (lower) than linear models.
Is it OK to claim that IRT models are more precise than linear ones and
more reliable when items are ordinal?
Sorry for my naive question...
MK

messages.subject: Re: mirt versus robust linear
parts:
On Thu, Apr 20, 2017 at 5:36 PM, Martin Kanovsky <martin....@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Phil,
thanks a lot for writing mirt, very useful and excellent tool...
I fitted 6-factor IRT model (graded response, MHRM).
Fit indices, especially SRMSR and RMSEA are very different in comparison
with robust linear methods (I supposed it, of course).
AIC and BIC of mirt models is always better (lower) than linear models.
These models aren't really nested, so comparing AIC and BIC estimates is not likely appropriate.

Is it OK to claim that IRT models are more precise than linear ones and
more reliable when items are ordinal?

That's hard to say. Linear approximations are going to be more 'efficient' when a linear approximation is good, while the IRT models are going to suffer in smaller sample sizes because the number of parameters are larger. So, like all good statistical questions, the answer is "it depends". 

Phil

Sorry for my naive question...
MK
